Query checks and independent reports

Unit 2 · Week 4 · Lesson 4 · Suggested 55-minute plan; adjust to local timing.

Prepare: Open a working copy of sql-starter.sqlite in a school-approved SQLite-capable application and locate its SQL editor. Alternatively execute sql-setup.sql once in a new empty database. Run one SELECT at a time. Use sql-workbook.md, sql-answers.md, sql-worked-queries.sql and sql-expected-results.json. The data are fictional. DueDate is valid YYYY-MM-DD TEXT and Returned is INTEGER 0/1 in this SQLite starter. Fixed reporting date: 8 April 2026. Teacher notes and answers are public.

Suggested answers are teacher guidance, not extra assessment tasks. These notes are public.

1. Query checks and independent reports

Suggested time: 2 minutes

Instructional strategy: Learning intention

Return to the earlier single-item Loan model. The reservation model was a separate normalisation exercise. This week uses SELECT queries to read data. Activities are ungraded. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#sql-basics.

2. A result that needs checking

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Recall and prediction

Check result columns, matching rows, counts and order. A missing comma can become an alias. A wrong Boolean condition can return plausible extra rows. Successful execution alone does not establish that the query meets the requirement. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#sql-basics.

3. Distinct result values

Suggested time: 6 minutes

Instructional strategy: Worked example

The result contains Camera, Microphone, Recorder and Tripod, four distinct description values. E01 and E04 still exist as separate stored items. DISTINCT applies to all selected result columns together, not just one chosen field. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#sql-basics.

4. Four description values

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Teacher model with predictions

The complete description result has four rows while Equipment contains five item records. If EquipmentID is selected as well, all five ID/description pairs differ and survive DISTINCT. DISTINCT does not delete stored records or fix a modelling problem. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#sql-basics.

5. A valid empty result

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Guided paired practice

This valid query returns zero rows, with an EquipmentID result column. Compare with a misspelt field such as EquipmentIdentifer, which is an error. First inspect whether any data should satisfy the condition. Missing values use IS NULL or IS NOT NULL, not = NULL; required starter fields contain no NULLs. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#sql-basics.

6. Four independent reports

Suggested time: 12 minutes

Instructional strategy: Independent application

Reports: borrower IDs/labels by ID; C03 equipment IDs/descriptions by ID; active loans newest due date first with LoanID ASC ties; active B002 LoanIDs by ID. Expected: B001–B004 labels; E03 Recorder and E05 Microphone; L004, L002, L006, L001; L002 only. Exact SQL and results are in sql-answers.md. Then complete workbook questions 6–10 for duplicate, empty and boundary checks. No scores or assessment records are required. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#sql-basics.

7. A query that looks plausible

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Misconception check with reasons

L005 belongs to B002 but Returned=1. Require Returned=0 AND BorrowerID='B002'. Check for a missing return-status condition, OR in place of AND or ungrouped OR alternatives. Compare expected L002 only with the actual result before editing. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#sql-basics.

8. An explanation with evidence

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Reflection and a fresh example

Examples: equal dates expose missing tie-break ordering; a returned row exposes an OR/filter error; selecting EquipmentID with a description exposes misunderstanding of DISTINCT; an empty match separates a valid query from a misspelt field. Record the SQL and predicted/actual outcome for self-review. Querying here remains single-table and read-only. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#sql-basics.
